turns.t: Mrs Okafor? Sorry about the rain, the lot is full today, so you'll want the validation stamp from me before you leave.
Oh, thank you, I parked on the street, two blocks over, I got soaked. Is this where Tobias goes, room four?
Yes, room four, the doctor's ready for you. Hi there, Tobias, love the dinosaur boots.
They roar.
Hello, you two. Come in, have a seat. What a day out there. Tobias, are those your rain boots?
Yeah. T-Rex.
Very scary. Okay, mom, what brings you in?
So he's got this rash all over his tummy and a bit on his back, it started two days ago, and I thought it was the new laundry soap, but then I switched it back.
All right. Two days. Does it bother him, does he scratch it?
Not much. Oh, and he's been cranky, but that's also because we had a birthday party Saturday, with way too much cake.
Ha, that'll do it. Tobias, can you show me where it is?
Here. And here.
Thank you, buddy. Mom, has he had a fever with it?
No, no fever. I checked this morning, and last night.
And any trouble breathing, or swelling of his lips or face?
No, nothing like that, thank goodness. His face is normal. He's been chasing the dog around all morning, so he's fine.
Good to know. Any medical conditions I should have on his chart?
He has asthma. Mild, since he was two. It's well controlled, mostly.
Okay. And who's at home with him, besides you?
My mother-in-law lives with us, so she watches him weekdays. She's obsessed with the weather, hence my umbrella.
Ha. Let me check his temperature and weight, then.
Temperature is 37.4 °C, and his weight is 17 kg.
Is that okay for four years old?
Right where he should be. Now, I want you to know what I'm thinking about, but I'm not putting a name on this yet.
That's fine. I just don't want it to get worse.
So here are the options. We could wait and watch for a few days, we could do a blood test to look at his counts, or we could get a specialist to look at the skin.
What would you pick?
I'd like to order a blood test today. It's quick, a tiny needle, Tobias, and it gives us information.
No needle.
Sweetie, it's just a tiny pinch, and there's a sticker after.
I have dinosaur stickers, actually. The lab's down the hall, I can walk you over when we're done.
Dinosaur?
A T-Rex one, I bet. In the meantime, cool cloths on the rash feel nice, and loose cotton clothes.
Okay. Cotton, cool cloths. Should I take photos of it?
Yes, take a photo each morning, that'll help me see whether it's changing.
Will do. And if his lips start swelling?
Then call 911 right away, don't drive him. But I doubt it'll come to that.
Okay. Thank you, doctor. And sorry for rambling.
Not at all. Tobias, you were great. Stickers on the way out.
Bye bye.

chief_complaint.value: he's got this rash all over his tummy

social_history.description: Lives with mother-in-law who watches him on weekdays

clinical_actions.description: Cool cloths, loose cotton clothes, daily photo of the rash; call 911 if lips swell
